ai.description: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* is a medium-sized gecko (SVL ~60 mm) with a pale brown body and dark transverse bands. It is distinguished by strongly keeled, trihedral dorsal tubercles and a serrated tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous row of enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles forming a lateral fold along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in the Aravalli and Satpura ranges, typically at elevations between 200 and 900 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* is a nocturnal gecko that remains active at night, foraging for insects on rocky outcrops and tree trunks within its native habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, extending from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus gujaratensis* is endemic to the Aravalli Range in Gujarat and Rajasthan, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 200 and 900 meters.
